L’Ecole étant engagée dans une démarche RSE (DD-RS et employeur pro-vélo), elle encourage aux mobilités douces par la mise en place de dispositif d’aide financière (FMD) et des infrastructures adaptées aux cyclistes ». Poste à temps complet (25 jours de congés annuels, 23 RTT annuels) Avantages : Transports (participation forfaitaire de l’employeur à hauteur de 75 %) Forfait mobilité durable (jusqu’à 300€/an) Possibilité de télétravail (après période d’essai et après accord du manager et dépôt d’une demande) Subvention employeur au restaurant administratif et/ou à la cafétéria de l’établissement Comité d’action sociale, avec notamment des événements et animations proposés au personnel, salle de sport sur adhésion, Mutuelle (participation à hauteur de 50% de l’établissement) Aménagement du poste de travail et recrutement inclusif : Tous nos postes sont ouverts aux candidats en situation de handicap. ENSTA s’engage à un recrutement favorisant l’égalité, la diversité et l’inclusion. Toutes les candidatures sans aucune distinction (âge, handicap, sexe, nationalité, religion, orientation sexuelle…) ont leur place dans notre processus de recrutement. Présentation de l’Ecole ENSTA est membre fondateur de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris) . Dans le cadre d’IP Paris, l’école participe aux activités des centres interdisciplinaires notamment du centre interdisciplinaire d'études pour la Défense et la Sécurité (CIEDS, soutenu par le ministère des armées et l’agence de l’innovation de défense (AID). Elle est à l’origine de la création du Centre interdisciplinaire Mers & Océans , inauguré en janvier 2025. Des chercheurs de l’école travaillent également en collaboration dans le cadre d'études portées par les centres Hi-Paris, lauréat en 2024 IA Cluster, E4C ou E4H notamment. ENSTA résulte de la fusion le 1er janvier 2025 d’ENSTA Paris et d’ENSTA Bretagne. Son siège est situé à Palaiseau (91), sur le campus de Paris-Saclay et elle a un autre campus à Brest. Elle met en place une nouvelle formation d’ingénieur unifiée sur les deux campus (Paris-Saclay et Brest) à la rentrée académique 2026/2027. Rejoindre l'école, c'est intégrer un établissement engagé pour la parité et l'égalité professionnelle, la diversité et l'accompagnement de ses agents en situation de handicap , dès le recrutement et tout au long de la carrière. Afin de préserver le bien-être au travail, l'école mène une politique active en matière de conditions de travail, reposant notamment sur un juste équilibre entre vie personnelle et vie professionnelle. Connaissances : Vous disposez des compétences suivantes : Formation supérieure en mécanique des fluides, énergétique, mécanique, génie maritime ou domaine équivalent. Solides connaissances en mécanique des fluides et en hydrodynamique navale. Expérience en simulation numérique des écoulements (CFD) et en analyse de résultats de calcul. Maîtrise d'au moins un langage de programmation scientifique (Python, C/C++, Fortran…). Compétences en traitement, analyse et visualisation de données scientifiques. Autonomie, rigueur scientifique, capacité à travailler en équipe et à conduire des campagnes de calculs et d'essais. Bon niveau d'anglais scientifique. Les compétences suivantes seraient appréciées : Compétences en méthodes particulaires, notamment en méthode SPH, ou intérêt marqué pour leur mise en œuvre. Expérience en expérimentation en mécanique des fluides. Connaissances en optimisation numérique et/ou optimisation de géométrie. Mesure des efforts en dynamique, en mouvement forcé à l’aide de l’hexapode : masses et inerties ajoutées, termes liés aux vitesses angulaires. Adaptation du code de calcul pour intégrer des lois de commande issues de mesures expérimentales. Enregistrement de l’historique des contrôles (vitesse hélice, angles plans porteurs, …), des trajectoires et des efforts des organes de contrôle. Tâche 6 – Rejeu trajectoires simulateur temporel Rejeu numérique des trajectoires, afin de valider si le modèle d’efforts est suffisamment complet pour prédire correctement les trajectoires mesurées expérimentalement. raw.title: SAP Analytics Consultant
raw.description:
We are seeking three experienced French-speaking SAP Analytics professionals to strengthen the internal SAP Finance/Analytics team of a public-sector client in Lausanne. The team supports the client’s financial reporting, budget planning, annual accounts and budget publication, all running on an SAP S/4HANA, BW / BW-IP, HANA and BusinessObjects landscape.

The three positions cover the full application lifecycle: one keeps the existing reporting and planning chains running, one builds enhancements and new developments, and one defines the target analytics architecture and guides the team through complex projects. All three work together within the same team, so you will have regular contact with colleagues across RUN, BUILD and architecture.

Location: Lausanne (minimum 3 days/week on-site during the first 3 months for onboarding and knowledge transfer, then remote. Remote work is possible only from Switzerland or the French border zone.

Contract: 01.01.2027 - 31.12.2029, renewable annually

Language: Fluent French

The Positions:

  1. SAP Analytics Techno-Functional Consultant – Corrective & Adaptive Maintenance (RUN) | approx. 100%

  • Qualify and analyse incidents on BW/IP, BO/Lumira, SLT, CDS/HANA Views and output management, including impact analysis

  • Reproduce issues and analyse data, performance, SLT replication and XML generation

  • Deliver corrections and changes across BW/IP, BO, Lumira, CDS/HANA, SLT and the custom ABAP XML program, with regression testing

  • Provide daily support for financial and budget reporting, as well as the production of annual accounts and budget publication

  • Deploy changes, support go-lives, carry out root cause analysis, and drive optimisation and documentation

2. SAP Analytics Techno-Functional Consultant – Enhancements & New Developments | approx. 60%

  • Analyse financial, budget and social reporting needs and map CRM/S4, BW, SLT and output management flows

  • Design BW/IP, HANA, CDS, BO/Lumira and SLT solutions and estimate effort and risks

  • Run POCs on analytical models, SLT and XML output flows

  • Build BW/IP models, CDS/HANA Views, BO/Lumira reports, SLT flows and the ABAP XML program, including testing

  • Prepare environments, transports and go-lives, and hand over to the support team

3. SAP Analytics Expert – Evolutive Maintenance & New Developments (mini-projects) | approx. 45%

  • Define the target analytics architecture (BW/IP, HANA, CDS, BO/Lumira, SLT) in line with the SAP roadmap and cloud analytics solutions

  • Lead scoping and GAP analysis, and deliver documented recommendations backed by SAP references and SWOT analysis

  • Lead POCs and validate performance and reporting output

  • Conduct design reviews, performance analysis and optimisation

  • Support the team on complex developments and knowledge transfer

Your Profile (all positions):

  • Senior-level SAP Analytics / BI experience on S/4HANA (for the Expert position: expert level, with proven experience in leading analytics architecture and design)

  • Strong BW / BW-IP skills in design, modelling, data loading, financial reporting and budget planning

  • Hands-on experience with financial reporting tools: AfO, BEx Analyzer, BEx Query Designer, WAD and broadcasting

  • Experience in budget planning, including planning models, simulations, consolidation and reporting

  • Solid knowledge of SAP BusinessObjects, Lumira and migration to WebI (N4V for WebI is a plus)

  • Experience with SAP SLT (CRM → S/4HANA replication, monitoring and troubleshooting)

  • Experience designing, extending and optimising CDS Views and HANA Views

  • ABAP skills to maintain and enhance a custom program generating XML for output management

  • Understanding of integration across CRM, S/4HANA, BW, HANA and reporting tools, with a focus on data quality, performance, security and governance

  • Knowledge of management accounting (controlling) and project management

  • Familiarity with RUN processes: incident resolution, SPS/SP cycles, regression testing, transports and Basis validation

  • Experience with Jira, ChaRM, Solution Manager and Confluence

  • Knowledge of SAP cloud analytics solutions (and, for the Expert position, the SAP analytics roadmap)

  • SAP Analytics certifications (BW, BW-IP, CDS Views, SLT, BO, Lumira, SAP cloud analytics) are an advantage

  • Fluent French is essential

What We Offer:

  • A long-term engagement through 2029, renewable annually

  • Meaningful work supporting the financial and budget processes of a public-sector organisation

  • A broad and modern SAP Analytics landscape covering BW/IP, HANA, CDS, SLT, BO/Lumira and cloud analytics

  • A choice of focus (RUN, BUILD or architecture) to suit your expertise and availability

  • Collaboration within an experienced internal SAP Finance / Analytics team

  • Remote working after the onboarding phase

  • Opportunities to shape the client’s analytics architecture and future roadmap

title: Growth & AI Marketing Operations Specialist
description: About Papers Papers AG is a Swiss cyber security engineering house and an incubator for our product portfolio. We build device-level alternatives to centralized cloud and trust. Our strategy is to grow our foundational decentralized network by building high-demand enterprise products directly on top of it. Your portfolio includes: Acurast: Decentralized confidential compute running on ordinary smartphones. Obsidio: A continuous, AI-assisted pentesting subscription. Incubated by Papers, Obsidio is built directly on Acurast, leveraging the decentralized network as a unique compute moat to battle-test networks. Hypergate: Enterprise mobile single sign-on for managed Android and iOS fleets. As an engineering-driven team, we work with autonomy and purpose. Our culture is built on meritocracy, long-term thinking, and a commitment to quality over buzz, innovation is in our DNA. We aim to collaborate with people who love tech for its own sake and want to help shape the future by solving real-world challenges. Your role We are seeking a tech-savvy, execution-oriented Growth & AI Marketing Operations Specialist to serve as the engine powering our growth campaigns, content infrastructure, and data analytics pipeline. Your main goal will be to communicate our stories across a portfolio of brands by bridging the gap between cutting-edge AI, data operations, and tactical growth marketing. You’ll be building automated content workflows, ensuring the highest quality across everything we generate, running multi-channel campaigns from start to finish, and maintaining rock-solid attribution tracking. If you are obsessed with efficiency, operational speed, and using AI to scale output without ever sacrificing quality and if you thrive when given a blank slate to write your own playbook, this role is for you. Success Metrics (First 90 Days) 30 Days: Take full ownership of the existing marketing tech stack and establish baseline performance metrics. 60 Days: Fully automate the core content generation pipeline and establish QA workflows. 90 Days: Launch at least two multi-channel growth experiments and demonstrate a measurable reduction in CAC or an increase in content throughput. Core Responsibilities 1. Storytelling That Converts Making Complexity Clear: Take complex, often highly technical capabilities and features and turn them into clear, digestible stories without losing accuracy. Audience-First Messaging: Understand who the campaigns speak to (developers, technical decision-makers, business stakeholders or end users) and frame each capability around what that audience cares about, at the right level of technical depth. Spark Curiosity & Action: Craft narratives that get audiences interested and excited, and that move them to the desired conversion. Product & Engineering Collaboration: Work closely with product and engineering teams to deeply understand what is being built, so every story is both compelling and technically correct. 2. Tactical Deployment & Agile Execution Multi-Channel Campaign Launch: Execute and launch integrated campaigns across communities, social channels, search, newsletters, loyalty programs, influencers, paid ads and landing pages. Where needed, bring in and coordinate additional third parties to support execution, such as external PR firms and campaign support providers. Marketing Automation: Maintain and scale lifecycle workflows, lead scoring mechanisms, drip sequences, and automated triggers to optimize lead conversion through the relevant funnel. Rapid A/B & Multivariate Testing: Design, set up, and evaluate rapid growth experiments (copy variants, landing page layouts, audience segmentation, offer positioning) on a weekly sprint cycle. 3. AI Pipeline Operation & Content QA Automated Workflow Orchestration: Build, maintain, and optimize AI-driven content pipelines to generate high-quality marketing assets at scale. Human-in-the-Loop Quality Assurance: Establish strict QA processes to review, refine, and approve AI-generated copy, visual assets, landing page content, and email sequences before deployment. Prompt Engineering & Template Optimization: Continuously iterate on, standardize, and version-control skills, design systems and context workflows to ensure output matches brand voice, compliance standards, and conversion best practices. Scale & Efficiency Metrics: Track content throughput, error rates, and time-to-market reduction, driving continuous improvement in pipeline efficiency. 4. Analytics, Attribution & Data Ops Tracking Infrastructure: Implementation and maintenance of event tracking, pixel setups, UTM parameters, and server-side tracking across all digital properties. Attribution Modeling: Own multi-touch attribution models to accurately trace pipeline generation, conversions, and revenue back to specific campaigns, channels, and AI-driven experiments. Data Integrity & Governance: Regularly audit marketing data across CRMs, marketing automation platforms, and internal databases to clean anomalies and maintain a single source of truth. Performance Reporting: Build and manage real-time dashboards providing actionable insights into CAC, LTV, conversion rates, and ROI across experiments. What We Are Looking For Essential Experience & Qualifications 3–5+ Years in Growth/Marketing Operations: Proven track record in a fast-paced B2B or B2C growth environment, managing campaign ops, marketing automation, and technical data pipelines. Passionate Builder: You deeply identify with our products. We are a fast-moving, mission-driven team, and this role requires intrinsic dedication rather than a standard 9-to-5 mentality. Hands-on AI Tooling Expertise: Demonstrated experience applying modern LLMs and generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, Higgsfield) into real-world marketing workflows, beyond simple basic prompts. Technical Analytics Proficiency: Deep hands-on experience with Google Tag Manager (GTM), Google Analytics 4 (GA4), and data visualization tools. Automation Skills: Proficiency with automation platforms to connect API endpoints and pass payload data reliably. CRM & Automation Platforms: Direct administration experience with platforms like Zoho. Preferred Technical Skills Basic technical understanding of Python, JavaScript, HTML/CSS for lightweight API scripting, data manipulation and rapid landing page iterations Mindset & Soft Skills Systems Thinking: Ability to map out complex, multi-step processes and translate business requirements into efficient technical architecture. Agile Adaptability: Comfort operating in fast-paced sprint cycles with changing priorities and a bias toward continuous shipping and learning. Obsessive Attention to Detail: An eagle eye for QA; AI speeds up production, but your judgment ensures quality control and brand alignment. Working Environment & Expectations Execution Velocity: We prioritize shipping experiments quickly, learning from real-world data, and iterating fast. Tooling Ownership & Independence: You will have complete autonomy over our stack. We expect you to proactively recommend and implement the best modern automation and AI solutions. You define the tools you need to win. Asynchronous Communication: Clear documentation, meticulous task tracking, and transparent status updates are core to how we work, allowing you to manage your own time effectively. Why join Papers? Work with cutting-edge technology that actually matters with a team that is obsessed with redefining what cutting edge means. High ownership, low bureaucracy. Your voice drives the strategy, giving you the independence to define your own processes. Influence the Growth strategy from day one. Competitive compensation structure tied directly to your impact, with clear pathways for career growth. 25 days paid vacation per year. Regular team events and retreats (at least quarterly). Support for your ongoing learning and development.r Find more English Speaking Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The role

AI is moving faster than any single product team can track. Nebius is expanding across serverless, databases, MLflow, MLOps, Physical AI, and HCLS — and customers arriving with complex, real-world ML workloads need more than documentation. This role exists to close that gap: someone who can prototype what's possible, accelerate customers through their first 90 days, and feed hard-won field insight back into the product roadmap.
This role sits at the intersection of deep ML engineering and product impact. You'll spend roughly half your time in the field — helping new customers move from POC to production, running technical onboarding, and working hands-on through their ML stack. The other half you'll spend building — prototyping applied AI use cases that show what's possible on the platform, going deep on emerging techniques before they're mainstream, and turning that expertise into concrete product direction.
This is not a presales role. You get your hands dirty every day.

What success looks like in 12 months

  • The product and sales teams have a library of working, polished demos they reach for on calls
  • Enterprise customers you've touched have meaningfully faster time-to-value than those you haven't
  • At least 2–3 product changes were shipped because of feedback you originated
  • The team understands where applied AI is heading 6–12 months from now, partly because you told them

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Build prototypes and demos across the product portfolio — serverless inference, databases, MLflow, MLOps, and vertical use cases in Physical AI and HCLS — that become assets for sales, product, and engineering teams
  • Support new customers hands-on through POC design, technical onboarding, and validation; act as the bridge between their ML team and the platform during the critical first months
  • Go deep on emerging applied AI — new training techniques, inference optimizations, agentic architectures, new frameworks — and turn findings into working prototypes, writeups, and product recommendations
  • Feed the product roadmap with specific, grounded feedback; be the voice of "here's what broke in three customer POCs last month and here's what needs to change"
  • Develop reusable technical assets — notebooks, reference architectures, benchmark results — that reduce onboarding friction at scale

We expect you to have:

  • You've fine-tuned large models, debugged distributed training jobs, built production RAG or agentic pipelines, and optimized inference on GPU infrastructure — not just read about it
  • You're fluent in the modern ML stack: PyTorch, HuggingFace, CUDA fundamentals, Kubernetes for ML, MLflow or equivalent, vector databases
  • You've worked with enterprise ML teams — whether as a solutions engineer, customer engineer, or an ML engineer who collaborated closely with customers
  • You read papers and implement them — not for credit, but because it's how you stay sharp
  • You communicate with calibration: you can explain activation checkpointing tradeoffs to an ML engineer in the morning and the cost implication to a CTO in the afternoon

It will be an added bonus if you have:

  • Experience in any of our vertical domains: Physical AI / robotics / simulation, HCLS (drug discovery, medical imaging, clinical NLP), or enterprise AI application development
  • Familiarity with MLOps at scale (Kubeflow, Metaflow, Argo, Ray)
  • Prior work at a cloud provider or AI infrastructure company
  • You've shared technical work publicly — notebooks, talks, blog posts that people actually use

Who thrives here

You'll thrive here if you're energized by variety — one day deep in a customer's MLOps stack, the next building a demo from scratch. You want your technical depth to influence product decisions, not just close deals.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
  • Opportunities for professional growth within Nebius.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • A dynamic and collaborative work environment that values initiative and innovation.

We're growing and expanding our products every day. If you're up to the challenge and are excited about AI and ML as much as we are, join us!

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

Base Compensation Range

$200—$350,000 USD

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. Our mission Build and scale the logistics capabilities that enable Mistral AI to deploy, operate and expand high-density compute infrastructure reliably. Own the flow, custody, traceability and readiness of high-value hardware, critical spares and associated materials - from supplier dispatch through site receipt, storage, deployment, repair and end-of-life disposition. Deliver speed without compromising safety, inventory integrity, security or cost control. Operating context & accountability You will coordinate closely with Data Center Operations, IT Operations, deployment teams, Procurement, Finance, Security, Safety, colocation operators, carriers and OEM service partners. The role owns Mistral logistics processes and supplier performance. Key responsibilities - deployment logistics and site readiness Plan inbound and outbound movements for accelerator servers, racks, networking equipment, CDUs, replacement parts, tooling and deployment consumables across sites and staging locations. Translate deployment schedules and bill-of-materials requirements into shipment plans, delivery windows, site receiving capacity, material availability and clear responsibility assignments. Coordinate with business partners and site teams on loading bays, access approvals, delivery routes, floor loading, rack handling, lift plans, packaging removal, temporary storage and installation sequencing. Identify logistics dependencies that could delay energization, commissioning, rack acceptance or compute availability; maintain escalation paths, contingency plans and recovery actions. Create consistent procedures for goods receipt, inspection, damage recording, quarantine, staging, pick/pack, handover and proof of delivery, including exceptions and nonconformances. Manage reverse logistics for defective equipment, repair exchanges, warranty returns, redeployments and end-of-life assets, with documented chain of custody and secure disposition. Key responsibilities - inventory, spares and asset traceability Define and maintain an accurate inventory and asset-control framework for Mistral-owned equipment, including serialized items, location, ownership, status, movement history and reconciliation with IT asset records. Set and monitor critical spare-parts policies with IT Operations and OEM partners: minimum/maximum stock, lead times, failure demand, replenishment triggers, shelf-life and obsolescence exposure. Establish auditable stock movements, cycle counts, physical inventories, discrepancy investigations and controls for high-value or sensitive components. Monitor stock health, aging, availability, stranded inventory, shrinkage and repair turnaround; use evidence to optimize local versus regional stocking decisions. Coordinate secure storage conditions, ESD-sensitive handling, environmental requirements, battery transport/storage rules where applicable, and restricted access to valuable hardware. Develop common inventory taxonomy, operating procedures and system integrations to support growth across sites, providers and countries. Key responsibilities - supplier, transport and commercial performance Oversee third-party logistics providers, freight forwarders, warehouses, specialist rigging partners and couriers against agreed service levels, security controls and escalation requirements. Work with Procurement and Legal on supplier selection, scopes of work, insurance, liability, transport terms and measurable performance expectations. Coordinate cross-border shipping requirements with qualified customs and trade-compliance specialists, including import/export documentation, duties, restricted goods and relevant sanctions/export controls. Monitor freight, warehousing, handling, repair and expedite costs; challenge avoidable spend while protecting deployment dates and service restoration capability. Lead supplier performance reviews, delivery-failure investigations and corrective action follow-up; develop alternative routes and providers for critical supply chains. Maintain reliable forecasting and reporting of expected arrivals, shortages, inventory exposure, blocked shipments, deployment readiness and outstanding returns. Key responsibilities - safety, resilience and cross-functional execution Partner with Safety and site teams to assess high-risk material handling, rack moves, lifting/rigging, traffic management and contractor interfaces; verify that required plans and competent resources are in place. Coordinate physical-security requirements, access permissions, tamper evidence and chain of custody for sensitive or high-value technology. Develop practical business-continuity plans for shipment disruption, customs holds, supplier shortages, loss or damage in transit, and urgent hardware replacement needs. raw.title: Design & Reliability Engineering Manager
raw.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

Our mission

Shape the engineering foundations of Mistral AI’s next generation of compute capacity while improving the resilience of the infrastructure already in service. This role combines technical design leadership with field reliability engineering: you will establish demanding, practical requirements for colocation power and cooling, scrutinize proposed solutions and turn operating experience into better designs, safer changes and more reliable AI capacity.

Operating context & accountability

Mistral deploys high-density AI infrastructure in colocation facilities, where partners operate the underlying critical plant. You will be Mistral’s technical counterpart to providers, designers, commissioning specialists and internal IT and capacity teams. The position combines forward-looking design authority with hands-on technical investigation and portfolio reliability improvement. It requires depth in one core engineering discipline and the judgment to lead multidisciplinary decisions with specialist support.

Key responsibilities — design and technical standards

  • Own and continuously improve Mistral’s technical design criteria and colocation requirements for new facilities, expansions and retrofits, including availability objectives, failure domains, maintainability and operational flexibility.

  • Translate GPU platform roadmaps into measurable facility envelopes: IT load and transients, rack density, electrical topology, redundancy, cooling capacity, supply/return temperatures, flow, pressure, water quality and monitoring.

  • Review utility and MV/LV arrangements, transformers, generators, UPS, switchgear, busway, protection coordination, earthing, power quality and metering for suitability under demanding AI loads.

  • Review mechanical and controls architecture, including chilled-water and heat-rejection systems, pumps, control sequences, CDU integration, leak detection, filtration, water treatment and cooling recovery scenarios.

  • Lead multidisciplinary reviews of single-line diagrams, P&IDs, sequences of operation, design calculations, capacity models, failure-mode studies and proposed deviations; document risks and decisions.

  • Participate in site selection, technical due diligence, provider RFPs, design milestones and commercial technical schedules, challenging assumptions before they become delivery constraints.

  • Define design review and exception processes that balance performance, resilience, deployment speed, efficiency, capital cost and long-term operability.

Key responsibilities — commissioning and delivery assurance

  • Partner with delivery and commissioning teams to define functional and integrated testing requirements, acceptance criteria, evidence packages and outstanding-defect management.

  • Validate that electrical and cooling infrastructure can support the contracted AI load envelope under normal, maintenance and credible fault conditions.

  • Review test scripts and results for loss of utility, UPS/generator transitions, cooling component failures, controls faults, CDU interface events and staged restoration where applicable.

  • Ensure operational handover includes accurate drawings, asset and interface registers, monitoring points, setpoints, maintenance constraints, emergency procedures and unresolved risk ownership.

  • Support live-site changes and capacity upgrades with a disciplined review of impact, sequencing, rollback plans and operational readiness.

Key responsibilities — field reliability and root-cause analysis

  • Act as a technical escalation point for recurring or high-impact electrical, mechanical and controls incidents across operational colocation sites.

  • Analyze alarms, BMS/EPMS trends, event sequences, power-quality records, cooling telemetry, commissioning findings and maintenance evidence to distinguish symptoms from systemic causes.

  • Lead or challenge technical root-cause investigations with colocation partners, including common-mode failures, protection miscoordination, thermal instability, control logic, hydraulic performance and hidden capacity limitations.

  • Develop risk-ranked corrective actions and reliability improvement programs; validate effectiveness through evidence and post-change monitoring.

  • Identify fleet-wide patterns and feed lessons learned into reference designs, acceptance tests, technical specifications and provider governance.

  • Review maintenance and change proposals that create material exposure to compute availability, providing clear technical recommendations and escalation where required.

Key responsibilities — collaboration and leadership

  • Work with IT hardware, network and platform teams to understand the operational consequences of rack-level and cluster-level failure domains.

  • Influence colocation providers, consultants and OEM partners through technically rigorous, fact-based reviews without relying on direct operational authority.

  • Present design trade-offs, reliability risks and investment recommendations in language accessible to engineering leadership and business stakeholders.

  • Develop reusable standards, technical playbooks and engineering knowledge sharing to support consistent decisions across a rapidly expanding portfolio.

What success looks like

  • New capacity is accepted against well-defined electrical, thermal and resilience criteria with transparent technical exceptions.

  • Design risks are identified early, reducing late changes, stranded capacity and avoidable operational constraints.

  • Repeat incidents and unresolved critical engineering defects decrease as corrective actions are verified.

  • Field experience produces measurable improvements to future designs and live-site operating resilience.

Minimum qualifications

  • At least 8 years in mission-critical data center design, engineering, commissioning or technical reliability, including responsibility for complex technical decisions.

  • Degree in electrical or mechanical engineering, or equivalent professional experience, with deep knowledge in one discipline and strong working knowledge of the other.

  • Demonstrated expertise in critical power and cooling architecture, redundancy, failure-mode analysis and operational risk management.

  • Experience reviewing engineering drawings, calculations, commissioning evidence and root-cause analyses, and coordinating technical specialists.

  • Ability to influence colocation providers and cross-functional stakeholders; excellent English communication and willingness to travel.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with AI/HPC infrastructure, high-density accelerator platforms and direct-to-chip liquid cooling.

  • Knowledge of CDUs, facility-to-technology cooling interfaces, hydraulic performance, cooling-water quality and leak management.

  • Experience with electrical protection/selectivity, power quality, controls sequences, integrated systems testing and BMS/EPMS analytics.

  • Experience creating technical standards across multiple sites or providers, including design deviations and fleet-wide reliability improvements.

  • Professional engineering registration or equivalent technical credentials.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

title: Senior Software Engineer, Add-Ons
description: Why Mozilla ? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. About this team and role: addons.mozilla.org (AMO) is the foundation of the Firefox add-ons ecosystem. It’s a showcase for developers to publish and grow their extensions, and a place of discovery for millions of users who customize Firefox to make it their own. Behind the scenes are the DevHub which enables developers to manage their extensions. To manage the ecosystem there are a series of Reviewer tools and automated moderation systems. As a Senior Software Engineer, you’ll bring a passion for crafting resilient systems that accelerate our review and moderation teams to provide a first-class experience for Add-on developers. You’ll work closely with engineers, reviewers, developer support, and Add-ons leadership to turn ideas into polished features, modernize the platform and its architecture, and see your work reach millions of people around the world. What you’ll do: Deliver major features and architectural improvements across the Add-ons stack, including automated moderation pipelines, Reviewer tools, and DevHub. Help establish and maintain engineering standards across areas such as code review, definition of done, production readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call practices, coding conventions, and infrastructure as code. Create robust observability systems and data-backed insights. Provide peer feedback, share knowledge and help others grow. Build and improve the systems that enable Add-ons engineering to safely develop, deploy, observe, and operate production services. Improve our CI/CD pipelines using declarative, pipeline-as-code approaches that make changes reproducible, testable, and easy to review. Deliver work iteratively using a visible backlog, short feedback cycles, retrospectives, and demonstrations to stakeholders. Write clear technical documentation, including design notes, Architecture Decision Records, runbooks, and incident write-ups. Work effectively in unfamiliar codebases, tracing requests and asynchronous jobs end-to-end to understand failures and identify opportunities for improvement. Collaborate with designers, product managers, QA, and community contributors to deliver end-to-end improvements. Contribute in the open through pull requests, code reviews, and discussions. Work on: Feature development: submission flows, trust and safety signals, DevHub and Reviewer tools modernization. AMO application systems: Work within our Python/Django, MySQL, React/TypeScript, and asynchronous processing systems. Internal developer platforms : Create tools and paved paths that make it easier for teams to ship and operate software safely and consistently. Team Process: Contribute to team ceremonies, execute process improvement, and provide feedback on team effectiveness. Engineering standards : Help make production readiness, testing, recoverability, documentation, and safe deployment part of the normal development lifecycle. Platform reliability: Deployments, monitoring, and incident response. What you’ll bring: Strong hands-on experience building and maintaining production applications with Python/Django. Experience operating and improving production software systems where reliability and safe delivery matter. Strong experience with CI/CD systems and treating pipelines and infrastructure declaratively as code. Experience designing or improving automated testing and deployment workflows, including integration testing and staged or progressive delivery. Strong understanding of observability as an engineering discipline, including metrics, logging, tracing, service-level objectives, and actionable alerting. Experience building or maintaining internal tools or platforms used by other engineering teams, with an understanding that internal systems have users, reliability expectations, roadmaps, and lifecycle considerations. Experience defining or improving engineering practices such as code review standards, operational readiness, runbooks, incident response, on-call expectations, or definitions of done. Ability to read and understand unfamiliar codebases and trace application behavior across frontend, backend, asynchronous jobs, data stores, and infrastructure. Experience debugging complex production issues and turning what you learn into lasting system improvements. Strong technical writing skills, with experience creating useful documentation such as design documents, ADRs, runbooks, and incident reports. Experience working iteratively with a visible backlog, regular stakeholder feedback, and retrospectives that result in concrete improvements. Strong collaboration and communication skills in a distributed team environment. A willingness to share knowledge and mentor peers in operational and reliability practices. Commitment to our values: Welcoming differences Being relationship-minded Practicing responsible participation Having grit Bonus points for: Experience with Google Cloud and operating Kubernetes. Experience with infrastructure-as-code tooling and policy-as-code. Experience establishing SLOs and error-budget-based reliability practices. Experience with chaos engineering, disaster recovery testing, or production readiness reviews. Experience with trust and safety, automated moderation, abuse prevention, or other adversarial systems. Contributions to open source projects What you’ll get: Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday One-time home office stipend Annual professional development budget Quarterly well-being stipend Considerable paid parental leave Employee referral bonus program Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) About Mozilla Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online. Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions. We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. Please contact us at hiringaccommodation@mozilla.com to request accommodation. We are an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate on the basis of race (including hairstyle and texture), religion (including religious grooming and dress practices), gender, gender identity, gender expression, color, national origin, pregnancy, ancestry, domestic partner status, disability, sexual orientation, age, genetic predisposition, medical condition, marital status, citizenship status, military or veteran status, or any other basis covered by applicable laws. Mozilla will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics or any other unlawful behavior, conduct, or purpose. title: Chief Technology Officer - US-Based
description: About Toptal Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe , Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce . We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold. Position Description: As Chief Technology Officer, you will drive execution for the product and engineering teams and put AI at the core of everything the company builds. You will own Toptal’s full technical architecture and you will build it AI-first—utilizing best practices for agentic engineering. AI is not a workstream inside the engineer team—its core to it. You will create and own the AI architecture and best practices the rest of the company utilizes. You will also own the initiatives that put agents into production. You should know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up, how to engineer best-in-class harnesses, and how to create best practices for agentic engineering that engineering teams adopt to 10x their productivity—without sacrificing quality. Your mindset will be that of a builder and an architect, someone who solves problems in the system itself. No problem will be too large or too small for you to solve yourself. You will set the technical direction and hold the cadenced meetings that turns technical strategy into working, production-ready outcomes. You will be in the design reviews and in the code, not adjacent to them. You will move fast, and you will ensure our engineering team is never the reason an initiative slows down. You are the technical owner of all Toptal’s products. You will collaborate closely with Product to design infrastructure that exposes Toptal’s core business logic through modular interfaces the rest of the business can build on. Alongside a group of hands-on executives, your engineering discipline directly shapes Toptal’s growth, profitability, and operational excellence. You will own resourcing and workforce planning as a doer: scoping the work, sizing the teams, planning headcount against it, defining the role and the bar for every seat. None of that is beneath the role, and we are not interested in someone who thinks these tasks can be done properly by handing it off to HR. Hiring is the highest-leverage work you do, and we want someone who is visibly excited about hiring A-players—with a sense of urgency. Then, you lead the team. You will set the standards, develop people against those standards, and know exactly who is meeting those standards. You will be one of Toptal’s foremost experts on AI, and you will stay ahead of a field that never stops moving. You will coach engineers on agentic best practices, show the executive team what is newly possible with the new AI tooling, and push AI into every function at Toptal. This role runs on high-energy execution and attention to detail. You will bring urgency to every part of it and measure yourself on outcomes. We are not looking for someone to oversee this work. We are looking for someone to drive it and get into the details. This is a remote position. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English. Responsibilities: The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills. One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction. AI and agentic engineering Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against. Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for. Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed. Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you. Team, resourcing, and accountability Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product. Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments. Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows. Platform and execution Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows. Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend. In the first week, expect to: Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services. Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO. In the first month, expect to: Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down. Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for. In the first three months, expect to: Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented. Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result. In the first six months, expect to: Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it. Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most. In the first year, expect to: Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering. Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan. Qualifications and Job Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred. 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale. Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up. Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work. Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence. Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers. Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for. You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI. Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar. Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale. Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield. Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself. You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do. Essential Job Functions Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera. Work independently with minimal supervision. Use all required digital collaboration tools. Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines. US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt Compensation Additional Information

One precondition runs through all of it: you conceive the strategy. You will form your own view of where engineering and AI should go, build the case, and bring the CEO a strategy to react to, not a request for direction.

AI and agentic engineering

  • Own Toptal’s AI technology strategy and the architecture beneath it: model selection and fine-tuning, harness design, orchestration, retrieval, context engineering, tool and MCP integration, guardrails, evaluation, and cost control, exposed as primitives every team composes against.
  • Deploy agentic engineering at scale against the work that runs this business: matching, vetting, onboarding, delivery, and internal operations. Own the outcomes those agents are accountable for.
  • Make AI quality measurable. Own the evals, the regression suites, and the review loops, so quality here is proven rather than claimed.
  • Rebuild how the platform gets built and operated, raising output per engineer through AI-assisted development, review, testing, and operations. Engineers have to want this, not comply with it, and creating that pull is on you.

Team, resourcing, and accountability

  • Decide what a team should look like now that the roles have blurred, where the product manager believes they can design and code, the engineer believes they can do product and design, and the designer believes they can code and do product.
  • Own resourcing and workforce planning: scope the roadmap into buildable work, plan headcount and sequence, write the specs, and hit time-sensitive hiring commitments.
  • Own the bar for the team: assess talent honestly, develop people against the bar, and hold it as the organization grows.

Platform and execution

  • Own the architecture end to end, from services and data flows to interfaces and system boundaries, and hold the standards that keep it coherent as it grows.
  • Own throughput, reliability, and the platform layer beneath them, including the AI-dependent paths where latency, drift, and provider outages are real failure modes. Own build-versus-buy, technical debt, secure-by-design architecture, responsible AI, and the engineering and AI cost structure down to inference and token spend.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Learn Toptal’s model and platform architecture, and meet the leaders you will depend on across Engineering, Product, Industries, and Services.
  • Establish a direct, working rhythm with the CEO.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Assess the engineering function honestly, and assess AI maturity with it: what is really in production, what is measured, what is duplicated, and what should be shut down.
  • Assess the team against the bar this role requires, and bring the executive team a strategy no one asked you for.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Be executing your own plan, with a review cadence and clear accountability at every level, and your resourcing plan presented.
  • Stand up the shared AI architecture and evals, and put one agentic workflow into production with a baseline and a measured result.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Show business impact from agents in production in at least two core workflows, with the evidence behind it.
  • Have the leadership team you need, with the bar visibly raised, and throughput and reliability moving on the paths that matter most.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Run an engineering organization recognized inside and outside Toptal as one of the most advanced in the industry, with the pull on AI now coming from engineering.
  • Have AI leverage embedded in the architecture and the operating model, not living in a portfolio of pilots, and the team you built delivering against plan.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field is required, and an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
  • 15+ years of progressive engineering leadership, including significant time as a CTO or VP of Engineering, or as a direct report to one at meaningful scale.
  • Deep, current, hands-on command of modern AI engineering: foundation models, agentic architectures, harness design, retrieval, context engineering, fine-tuning, and evaluation. You have shipped and operated these in production, and you know how to build and fine-tune foundation models from the ground up.
  • Agentic systems deployed at scale against real business processes, with measured outcomes on cost, cycle time, quality, or revenue, and a record of retiring what did not work.
  • Rigor about evaluation. You can explain precisely how you knew a model, prompt, or agent change was an improvement, and you can show the evidence.
  • Command of the economics underneath it: model routing, hosted versus self-hosted, inference capacity, latency and cost budgets, and staying portable across providers.
  • Further ahead on AI than the executives around you, able to teach it, and proven at moving an organization to adopt something it was not asking for.
  • You create strategy rather than administer it, and you win arguments on evidence rather than authority, including your view on what a team should look like in the age of AI.
  • Proven ownership of resourcing and workforce planning, and a hiring track record you can quantify. You have made the hard calls when someone was not clearing the bar.
  • Currently hands-on. You read and write code, you can take apart a design document or an eval harness and find the flaw in it, and you command distributed systems, service architecture, data-intensive applications, and cloud infrastructure at scale.
  • Experience scaling and modernizing a large existing codebase without stopping the business. You have replaced load-bearing systems in flight, not only built greenfield.
  • Experience leading a globally distributed, remote team at a technology or hyper-growth company is required. A high-volume, two-sided marketplace or multi-tenant platform is a significant plus.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Speed, ownership, and quality. You move with urgency, decide without perfect information, and treat everything you deliver as a reflection of yourself.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

title: Chief Architect
description: Chief Architect Remote - US Legion Technologies is building the AI-powered operating system for the hourly workforce. We are hiring a Chief Architect to serve as Legion’s most senior hands-on technical leader and to shape the technical foundation that will power the next decade of product innovation. This is not a strategy-only or advisory role. The Chief Architect must live close to the code, go deep with engineering teams, challenge assumptions, write and review technical designs, make high-consequence architecture decisions, and help turn bold product ambitions into scalable, reliable production systems. This person will own architecture and technical decision-making for the most complex parts of Legion’s Workforce Management platform, including AI, optimization, forecasting, scheduling, distributed systems, data platforms, real-time decisioning, enterprise scalability, security, compliance, and developer productivity. The ideal candidate has built and scaled mission-critical software used by large enterprise customers, has deep technical credibility with senior engineers, and can operate fluidly between code-level decisions and long-term platform strategy. They are pragmatic, decisive, opinionated, and comfortable making hard tradeoffs when simplicity, scalability, reliability, or customer trust require it. This role reports to the Head of Product, Engineering, and Support. This is an open role currently being filled on an interim basis by the CEO. Responsibilities and Duties Hands-On Architecture and Technical Decision-Making Serve as Legion’s senior-most hands-on technical authority for complex architecture, system design, and platform evolution. Personally dive into code, design documents, production incidents, performance bottlenecks, and implementation tradeoffs to diagnose root causes and guide technical direction. Lead the hardest technical decisions across AI systems, optimization engines, distributed systems, data architecture, reliability, scalability, security, and platform modernization. Write prototypes, reference implementations, architecture decision records, technical specifications, and design patterns where needed to unblock teams and establish clear direction. Make high-consequence technical decisions with incomplete information, balancing correctness, simplicity, speed, scalability, reliability, cost, and long-term maintainability. Challenge architectural drift, unnecessary complexity, weak abstractions, and short-term decisions that create long-term platform risk. Partner directly with Staff, Principal, and senior engineering leaders in design reviews, code-level discussions, and implementation planning. Platform Architecture and Technical Vision Define and own the long-term architecture for Legion’s AI-driven Workforce Management platform across application services, data infrastructure, ML systems, optimization engines, APIs, integration architecture, developer platforms, and enterprise-scale operations. Establish engineering-wide standards for system design, scalability, performance, reliability, extensibility, observability, security, and maintainability. Serve as the final architectural authority for major platform initiatives and technical decisions with long-term consequences. Identify opportunities to reduce complexity, improve system efficiency, accelerate engineering velocity, and unlock new product capabilities. Proactively surface technical debt, architectural risk, and platform constraints before they compound into customer, product, or engineering velocity issues. Create pragmatic migration paths from current-state architecture to target-state architecture while maintaining uptime, customer trust, backward compatibility, and delivery speed. Ensure Legion’s architecture supports enterprise configurability and extensibility without allowing uncontrolled customization or product fragmentation. AI, Optimization, and Decision Systems Architect AI-native product capabilities across forecasting, scheduling, labor optimization, recommendations, copilots or agents, anomaly detection, decision automation, and other intelligent workforce management use cases. Define the architecture for production AI systems, including data pipelines, feature platforms, model training, model serving, retrieval, evaluation, monitoring, feedback loops, and continuous improvement. Make clear build-versus-buy decisions across LLMs, classical ML, optimization solvers, retrieval systems, evaluation frameworks, and internal AI platforms. Partner closely with Product, Data Science, and Engineering to turn mathematically complex labor optimization problems into reliable, scalable, explainable production systems. Establish standards for AI system quality, including accuracy, latency, cost, explainability, drift detection, reliability, customer-specific behavior, and production observability. Ensure Legion’s AI capabilities remain differentiated, defensible, enterprise-ready, and deeply integrated into operational workflows rather than bolted on as superficial features. Distributed Systems, Data, and Enterprise Scale Drive architecture for large-scale, multi-tenant SaaS systems serving complex enterprise customers with high availability, performance, security, and compliance expectations. Lead technical decisions involving microservices, APIs, event-driven architecture, distributed data processing, real-time systems, data governance, and large-scale analytics. Improve the architecture for observability, incident analysis, performance engineering, capacity planning, reliability, and operational excellence. Use production data, incidents, escalations, and customer operational patterns as inputs into architecture and platform improvement. Ensure architectural decisions support global scale, data residency, enterprise integrations, configurability, extensibility, and long-term platform leverage. Product, Business, and Customer Impact Connect technical decisions directly to customer value, product velocity, implementation speed, scalability, reliability, and long-term platform advantage. Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to translate ambitious product goals into executable architecture and technical roadmaps. Understand enterprise customer complexity and design systems that support real-world operational variability without creating unsustainable technical debt. Support strategic customer, partner, and vendor architecture discussions where deep technical credibility is required. Help evaluate technical implications of major product, partner, platform, and commercial decisions. Engineering Culture and Technical Talent Mentor and elevate Staff Engineers, Principal Engineers, architects, and senior engineering leaders across the organization. Raise the bar for technical judgment, system design, architecture reviews, documentation, code quality, operational discipline, and engineering craftsmanship. Help assess, attract, and develop senior technical talent, including Staff, Principal, and architect-level engineers. Build a culture of disciplined technical thinking, direct debate, clear decision-making, and pragmatic execution. Ensure architectural decisions are documented clearly, understood broadly, and translated into executable engineering plans. Security, Compliance, and Enterprise Readiness Own the architectural approach to enterprise security, data governance, privacy, compliance, auditability, and resilience. Ensure architecture supports SOC 2, ISO 27001, data residency, access control, tenant isolation, regulatory requirements, and other needs of large global enterprise customers. Partner with Security, Infrastructure, Product, and Engineering teams to make security and compliance foundational architectural properties rather than after-the-fact controls. Travel Requirements Up to 15% travel for leadership collaboration, engineering offsites, strategic customer engagements, and other business-critical meetings. Required Skills and Qualifications Experience Level 15+ years of experience building and scaling large-scale software systems. Prior experience as a Chief Architect, Distinguished Engineer, Principal Architect, very senior Principal Engineer, or equivalent senior technical leadership role. Demonstrated success designing and scaling mission-critical, multi-tenant SaaS platforms for enterprise customers. Deep hands-on experience with large-scale distributed systems, cloud-native architecture, data platforms, APIs, event-driven systems, platform engineering, and high-availability production environments. Proven ability to operate as a hands-on technical leader who can credibly engage in code-level and design-level discussions with senior engineers. Experience making major architecture decisions for systems with high scale, high reliability requirements, complex domain logic, and long product lifecycles. Experience modernizing large production systems incrementally while maintaining uptime, backward compatibility, customer trust, and engineering velocity. Experience building or supporting AI, ML, optimization, decisioning, forecasting, or data-intensive products in production. Strong understanding of observability, incident response, performance engineering, reliability architecture, capacity planning, and operational excellence. Ability to communicate complex technical concepts clearly to engineering teams, executives, customers, and cross-functional partners. Technical Depth Deep expertise in distributed systems, system design, cloud architecture, service-oriented or microservices architectures, APIs, event-driven systems, and large-scale data processing. Strong experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure. Strong experience with modern engineering practices, including architecture reviews, design documents, code reviews, testing strategy, deployment architecture, observability, and production operations. Experience with languages such as Java, Kotlin, Go, Python, Scala, or similar modern backend languages. Ability to reason deeply about tradeoffs involving performance, latency, throughput, cost, reliability, developer productivity, extensibility, and maintainability. Leadership and Judgment Strong architectural judgment: knows when to simplify, when to re-platform, when to tolerate debt, and when to force a hard technical reset. Demonstrated ability to make bold technical decisions with incomplete information and drive alignment across senior technical and executive stakeholders. Ability to influence without relying on hierarchy, while still being willing to make clear decisions when consensus is insufficient. Strong product and business judgment; able to connect architecture decisions to customer outcomes, implementation speed, product differentiation, and company strategy. Pragmatic builder mindset: balances long-term architecture with startup speed, customer urgency, and execution realities. Preferred Qualifications and Attributes Experience building platforms used by millions of users or supporting very large-scale enterprise operations. Experience at companies known for large-scale distributed systems, AI, cloud infrastructure, enterprise SaaS, workforce management, supply chain, fintech, commerce, logistics, or other complex operational domains. Familiarity with optimization engines, scheduling algorithms, forecasting systems, constraint solvers, real-time decision systems, or mathematically complex production systems. Experience architecting AI-native product capabilities, including LLM-enabled workflows, AI agents or copilots, model evaluation, retrieval systems, feedback loops, and production monitoring. Experience building internal developer platforms, platform infrastructure, data platforms, ML pipelines, or large-scale analytics systems. Experience designing highly configurable enterprise platforms without creating unbounded customization or implementation complexity. Experience participating in strategic customer architecture reviews or technical due diligence with large enterprise customers. Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related technical field; PhD a plus but not required. Candidate Profile The strongest candidate will be a deeply technical, hands-on architect who still has the range to shape company-level technical direction. They are not a generic enterprise architect, process owner, or strategy-only leader. They are a builder and technical decision-maker who can personally engage with Legion’s hardest problems and earn the respect of the strongest engineers in the company. They should be comfortable moving between: Code and architecture. Product ambition and technical feasibility. AI innovation and production reliability. Startup speed and enterprise-grade rigor. Long-term platform strategy and immediate technical execution. They should be opinionated but not dogmatic, decisive but not reckless, and pragmatic without accepting mediocrity. They should be able to simplify complex systems, identify the real technical risks, and force clarity where teams are stuck in ambiguity. Compensation and Benefits Salary Range: Base Salary Range $300,000- $385,000 + Bonus + Stock Equity. At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data. Our posted salary range is done in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate's region, town, or cost of living. We strive to make competitive offers that allow employees room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount budgeted internally, and internal equity for the same position within the company. Benefits include, but are not limited to: $0 monthly premium and other flexible medical, dental, and vision plans effective on the first day of employment. 401k plan. Discretionary Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays. Parental Leave. Equity. Monthly Wellness Reimbursement. Monthly Lunch on Legion. ABOUT LEGION Join Legion's mission to turn hourly jobs into good jobs. We're a remote, mission-driven team seeking exceptional talent to propel this vision. Embrace a culture that's collaborative, fast-paced, and entrepreneurial. With us, you'll grow your skills, work closely with experienced executives, and contribute significantly to our mission. Legion Technologies delivers the industry’s most innovative workforce management platform. It enables businesses to maximize labor efficiency and employee engagement simultaneously. The award-winning, AI-driven Legion WFM platform is intelligent, automated, and employee-centric. It’s proven to deliver 13x ROI through schedule optimization, reduced attrition, increased productivity, and increased operational efficiency. Legion delivers cutting-edge technology in an easy-to-use platform and mobile app that employees love. If you're ready to make an impact and grow your career, Legion is where you belong. Join us in making hourly work rewarding and fulfilling. BACKGROUND AND OPPORTUNITY There are almost 75 million hourly workers in the United States, representing more than half of the entire workforce. Historically, managing hourly employees has been difficult due to high attrition (average of 60%) and high replacement costs (average of $3,200 per employee in retail). The ongoing labor shortage and competition from the gig economy make it more difficult to attract and retain hourly employees. The top reasons hourly employees leave their jobs are a lack of schedule empowerment, poor communication with employers, and an inability to get paid early. Gen Z and the millennial workforce demand gig-like flexibility, modern technology, and compelling work options. Legion’s mission is to turn hourly jobs into good jobs, serving the hourly workers who make up the majority of the US workforce. We believe in empowering employees and helping employers be efficient and innovative by enabling intelligent automation powered by Legion’s Workforce Management platform to optimize labor efficiency and enhance the employee experience simultaneously. Legion WFM was built for the cloud with AI at the core and designed to handle the complexity of modern businesses and meet the needs of today’s hourly employees. Our team is comprised of dedicated individuals from all backgrounds and experiences, globally distributed across all time zones. For more information, visit https://legion.co EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY Legion Technologies is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer and is committed to maintaining a diverse and inclusive work environment.
